idiom_name: abstract record Result<T, TError> with nested sealed Ok/Err and a switch expression
implementation_notes: C# has no Result in the standard library and its native error channel is exceptions, so the pattern is a hand-written contract. Records and switch expressions make the classic structure small: an abstract record Result<T, TError> with nested sealed Ok(T value) / Err(TError error) cases, a Match method or a switch expression for exhaustive-looking consumption, and factory or implicit-conversion helpers so a fallible call reads naturally. Records supply value equality for the result itself; exceptions stay for programmer errors and exceptional faults, converted at the boundary where the framework throws so the core never throws for expected failures. This is manual work (factories, helpers, conversion operators), which is why the library variant exists.
pitfalls: Nested generic case names (Result<T, TError>.Ok) must repeat the type arguments at every use site or inference produces confusing errors; a non-generic wrapper or static factory class removes the noise.
An Err whose failure value is an exception compares by reference even inside a record, so failure equality must come from the error model, not from record identity.
Implicit conversions from T to Result hide the Err construction that should stay explicit at the boundaries where failures are introduced.

variants.name: ErrorOr<T> library (fluent discriminated union)
variants.implementation_notes: ErrorOr<T> packages the hand-rolled structure as a fluent discriminated union: IsError/IsSuccess/Value/Errors observers, Then and ThenDo/ThenEnsure for chaining fallible steps, FailIf for guards, Else/ElseDo for recovery and Match/Switch (plus MatchFirst variants) for terminal handling, with a built-in catalog of error types (Validation, NotFound, Conflict, Unauthorized and so on) and implicit conversion from T. The Then chain is the railway in method syntax and keeps handlers thin, which suits request pipelines; the cost is that every intermediate step in a chain must itself return ErrorOr, so the type spreads through the layer it is adopted in. Keep the dependency at the application boundary and the domain types free of it.
variants.idiom_name: ErrorOr<T> with Then / FailIf / Else and Match
pitfalls: Then/FailIf chains read fluently but require every step to return ErrorOr, spreading the dependency; convert to it at the application boundary, not in domain types.
Match and MatchFirst overlap: choosing MatchFirst silently handles only the first error when several were accumulated.
